2023 Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat Fails To Sell Despite Just 252 Miles on the Clock
26 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The market for used Hellcat-spec Durango SUVs is a bit wobbly right now. It's hard to get a sense of where you're at, especially if you're trying to sell a low-mileage example. For instance, we've seen both sub-$70k and $80k+ valuations this year, depending on mileage, and one particular model that seems pretty much identical to this one, sold for $67,500 back in May.
To be fair, that was a 2021 model year vehicle, and this one is 2023MY - acquired new for $133,835 by the same person who tried to get rid of it at auction these past few days. Sadly, the reserve wasn't met, which comes as a surprise if I'm being honest. The top bid stood at $72,500 and clearly that wasn't enough. Why? I have no idea. There's no way this is an $80,000 SUV right now.
Maybe the seller was hoping for $75,000, but even that feels like a bit of a stretch. And yes, I did factor in the mileage (252 miles). I still wouldn't have held out for $75,000. Not just because it's a "hard sell", pun intended. But also because on top of the $72,500 bid, you need to factor in the buyer's fee, shipping and whatnot.
There's also an issue with high-performance SUVs in general when it comes to long-term collectibility and value retention. There's a massive difference between a vehicle that impresses you today, when it's new or just a few years old, and one that people dream of owning 15-20 years from now. I'm not sure any modern-day SUV, regardless of brand and performance, will be as desirable in the future as it is today.
People collect classic Mustangs and Chargers, not Willys Jeeps and C/K Chevys. I mean, they collect those too, but they don't spend fortunes on them, and they certainly don't dream about one day owning one.
Anyway, specs-wise, this Durango comes with Gunmetal over-the-top stripes spread across the Destroyer Gray (PDN) colorway, to go with a sunroof, bi-function LED headlights, a vented hood, roof spoiler, power-operated liftgate, plus a set of Lights-Out 20" alloy wheels rocking Pirelli P Zero rubber and red-finished calipers. The vehicle also comes with adaptive damping suspension, four-wheel traction control, Ready Alert Braking (RAD), and Trailer Sway Control.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the heated and ventilated front seats, heated second-row bucket seats, folding third-row seats, silver accent stitching throughout the cabin, a ParkView rearview camera, three-zone automatic climate control, adaptive cruise control, a Harman Kardon sound system, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel with paddle shifters.
As for the engine, it's a supercharged 6.2-liter HEMI V8 , good for 710 horsepower and 645 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via a TorqueFlite eight-speed automatic gearbox.
The Durango SRT Hellcat is capable of hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in about 3.5 seconds, before covering a quarter mile in just under 12 seconds. Technically, this is an 11-second SUV.
